I'm not the type into platformer game as you can see on my profile. But Strangely, I pick this one up from all great platformer game out there on steam.  The reason I pick this up because when I watch the trailer. I stun by its visual and music. Then I watch other trailer including prologue and gameplay, I feel more grow interested. It feels like there are all great things in there from graphic, music, sound effect, story and challenging gameplay. So I pick this up right away after the first launch. After finish about 10 hours play, I admit to say this game is absolutely FANTASTIC.
And I also not the type person who wanted to review some game. It takes time to write since english isn't my first language. But I take my time to write this short review cause this game deserves it.
Story
------
The game has some story cutscene as you progress through game. The story is about trying to restore the elements of nature in order to revive the tree of life after it has been attacked by dark giant owl. Although I think the story is kinda general but there are some emotional moment through the story will make you awe
Gameplay
------------
The controller is quite responsive. it has some moves you can do on this game like attack, jump, climb, glide, swim,  bash (like jump over) on enemy or projectile as you progress the game. All these moves require some thinking and good skill in order to pass some certain level. It will feel frustated hard at some try but eventually you get pass once you learn how. you also gain ability points to spend on simple ability skill tree for better experience during gameplay. The great thing of the gameplay that you use your resource like mana to create save and checkpoint. Meaning you can create checkpoint wherever you like except on some location.
The game has no  Bosses fight. In exchange they did some certain level which you need to escape before the times run out like climbing on top before the flood of  water rises up. The best part of this game is that there are no loading on each map or level. It gives you freedom to explore. So you can revisit the map when you miss something
Graphics and animation
----------------
Visual is absolutely stunning. The background is incredibly well drawn. Each location has different style and mood as you progress. The animation is also good and fluid. It makes the background feels alive. The main character Ori also has pretty well done animation. What I find impressive that the dev even add Ori has alternate jump animation. Overall this is truly the art that will appeal all the audience
Music and sound
-------------------------
Music is by far is the key to make this game so good. Each moment, the music fits very well. Like the moment when you try escape. This is what make me like this game more. Without this, I won't bother to retry the level after failed on so many try. That said the music absolutely amazing.
Sound effect probably is another addition makes this game looks so shine. like the big black owl stomp when landing on the ground, it feels so tremble. And also Ori has some cute voice when got hurt and surface from water to get air.
Closing thought
----------------------
Although this game has no high replayability but when I finished it, No doubt this game will become the 3rd best memorable game to me after 2 other games, Okami and Shadow of Collossus.

I've been staying away from most action games for years, focusing mainly on RPGs, but this game was great enough to make me retrain and enjoy again my ancient skills in platformers, puzzles (including those requiring the use of companion skills), bullet hells, sidescrollers and beat'em ups, with a bit of fighting and rhythm games throw in to spice things up as well. There were tactical RPG battles too and lots of card game playing, all within the framework of a great time travel RPG story with good characters and beautiful art (in gameboy, 8 bit, 16 bit and 3D styles). Depending on how rusty you are, some action portions of the game, and some puzzles, can be frustrating for a while (even at the lowest difficulty) only to cause that rush of satisfaction when you finally beat them. And there's enough variety of classical gameplay challenges that they don't get old. Difficulty adjustment changes things in interesting ways, can be tuned at any point in the game and is usually enough to keep things interesting. This was also the first game I ever got all achievements for (and I played the last half of it with my right arm in a cast!). I did it before the final boss fight, but you can actually go back to the game after it's over to wrap things up if you want. All in all, unless you really hate even small and well-rewarded amounts of frustration while playing, you really should give this game a try, particularly if you played those classics (and even if you, like me, think you no longer enjoy those).

Oddworld: New 'n' tasty:  Is a remake of the game 'Abes oddworld' featuring greatly improved graphics.
Graphics aside, This game features a very good single player experience with a good story and solid Action-puzzle platforming gameplay which seems to not resemble any other game i've played or heard of.
The game has you roam around as 'Abe' who is attempting to save his fellow race known as the Mudokens from slavary through the use of voice guiding e.g. "follow me" or "wait here". In order to navigate through the games hostile areas, you must use a combination of puzzle solving and quick reflexes as your character can die very quickly and can only attack through the use of the enviromoment, hypnotising enemies or using grenades and the
, and all cannot be used with ease, for example, you can only hypnotise one type of enemy known as sligs and only if there is no sercurity drone preventing you from doing so. as for grenades and the
you rarely obtain these through out the game and the grenades can only really be used when you are undetected. all these factors give you a unique and challenging experience that most will enjoy.
The game also features plenty of secret areas which you need to find if you want 100% completion.
When it comes to changes between the original and the remake aside from the graphics and the smooth sidescrolling as appose to screen by screen scrolling of the original, you wont find many differences between the two. most areas remain the same as far as I can tell with a few minor changes here and there that dont make any difference to how you solve each segment of the game. The game does add a quick save feature which you obviously dont have to use if you want the game to be as close to the original as possible. there is also a difficulty selection which changes how much damage you can take but before you panic, hard difficulty does replicate the original games one shot and your dead level of difficulty. The game also features a new voice command "all of ya" which simply allows the commanding of multiple mudokens at once
There arn't really any flaws with the game other than fellow mudokens being difficult to command correctly sometimes and the AI acting weirdly at times.
If you're looking for a game that offers unique and challenging gameplay then I recommend this game to you.

So, I got this game with a bundle, and probably never would have bought it otherwise. I figured it was a going to be a bunch of different game styles all mashed together with a lot of references and jokes about other games, and that overall it would feel kind of shallow and disjointed. I was half right.
It IS a bunch of random stuff thrown together, and it DOES have tons of references and jokes, and the gameplay is kind of shallow at points, and each of the mechanics are good but not as polished as they could be if the whole game had been made around them.
BUT
The mechanics are all solid and even though they're all kinda middle of the road individually, the way they're put together and the overall style and feel of this game is absolutely great. I fell in love with this game more and more as I got into it. I even went all the way and %100'd it, which I literally haven't done with a game in...decades? (Man I'm getting old)
It's not a hardcore RPG and it's very forgiving, but it gives you the same feeling as the classics without all the drag. It's never grindy, and it's pretty much always clear about what you need to do. There are lots of fun extras and discoverables, and I even kind of liked the trading card game (which I normally HATE in games). And despite it being essentially a collection of gaming tropes, the design and the writing make it feel fresh and pretty unique.
The only critique I really have in the end is that it could use a bit more proof-reading. There were a good amount of typos in the dialogue. But seriously, that's about all I can nit-pick on, so...yeah, well done.
Oh, and if you want more of a challenge there are different game modes. I was playing on "Adventure", and I get the feeling the other ones are harder? Don't know, didn't try it, but it's there.

It's this game's charm that made it a blast to play through for me. If your into plenty of video game references and changing game mechanics (with some portions of the game showing off more polish than others), this game is well worth a purchase.

Sadly I can't recommend this game to anyone. I haven't had the chance to play the first game, but I heard good things about it and I was really hoping that Epic Mickey 2 will be a great 3D platformer, but it's far from it, especially on PC.
The first thing I noticed that the game feels clunky. It often feels like a game from the era when developers were still just experimenting with the idea of 3D in a platformer and often times those games just doesn't feel right. It's something like that here, quite often I couldn't tell wheter an item is behind me or in front of me and if so how far. It's hard to explain, but the 3D just doesn't feel right compared to other games. There are 2D levels as well, but those are mostly really short (and I DO mean really short, 1-3 minutes mostly...).
That's the least of my worries though with this game, there are much bigger ones as well sadly. The PC port is just bad. Both optimization/graphics and control-wise. Especially the latter, the controls are terrible with keyboard+mouse. I pretty much always prefer to play my games with kb+m, but I'd really recommend using a gamepad if you really want to play this game (which you shouldn't).
...and lastly what really killed the game for me that it's basically a coop game that you can play alone as well and it just doesn't work well in solo. The AI is the worst I've seen since the late '90s. Oswald never does what you want him to do, never around when you need him and pretty much just runs around aimlessly while you wait for him so you can proceed with the game. I wouldn't even bother playing this alone to be honest, the AI pretty much killed all the fun.
All in all Epic Mickey 2 is the shoddy port of a mediocre game with terrible AI. It might be fun if you can get someone to play this with you (using controllers), otherwise skip this one, there are better platformers out there.

This is a game that was ment for consoles, and it really shows with many things.  Such as the keyboard controls. These controls are some of the most awful controls I've seen in a video game yet. That's why you should NOT pick up this game unless you have a Xbox 360/PS3 controller. Also, to just nitpick here, you can't go into full screen, which is very annoying on PC games. Now besides the port problems, this game has some extremely annoying characters such as Gus, the little green thing that wont ever shut up. He is constantly holding your hand through every little part of the game that may require you to think, which not only makes him an annoying character, but he also near ruins the game. That's another thing about this game: There is no challenge what so ever. The boss battles are the only thing that could be considered semi-challenging, and there are about 3 in the entire game, meaning the majority of the game is easy. Also, the game feels like DLC for Epic Mickey 1 more than anything, since it is so short. Really, you could probably beat the game in LESS THAN AN HOUR. Imagine purchasing a broken $60 game that only lasts 40 minutes. I'd be pretty♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off. Other complaints I had where the voice acting. Now I suppose you could probably deal with it, but really, the acting is pretty bad in this game. As well as the musical segments. Yep, musical segments. This game was marketed as a musical game, but really there are about 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥ songs in the entire game that are all sung by the same character. I wouldn't qualify this a musical. Now there are a few things I liked about the game. One of them being the boss battles. The battles brought in a change to the game, allowing you to choose how you defeat them: Turning them into a friendly,  or killing them. I though this was a great idea in Epic Mickey 1 and it is still a great idea in Epic Mickey 2. However, other games have done this practice MUCH better than Epic Mickey, because in this game, your choices don't really matter. If you pick the good choice, you are praised as a hero in the end. If you pick the bad choice, you are praised as a hero in the end. Though that doesn't really take away from the over all enjoyment of the fight. Another thing I liked was the enviroment. If you didn't know, the world is pretty much a destroyed Disneyland, however, the first game did this much better. On consoles this was an over all decent game, on PC however, it is a bad game. So if you want to play one of these games, GET THE THE FIRST ONE, or purchase this game on consoles. I still do recommend getting the first one, because it is a pretty good game, and it will help you understand this one better.

This game was part of a bundle I bought 1 year ago - together with Memoria and Dark eye: Chains of Satinav. I did not install it at the time because the looks of the game did not appeal to me at first. I even thought back then that this was a strategy game (its actually a turn based RPG :P)
One month ago, I decided to install the game in order to get the steam cards. Based on the reviews I was expecting a pretty aweful game. Nevertheless, I decided to play for an hour instead of idling.
The first screen I encountered was the character creation. I was pleasantly suprised by the depth and variety of choices and I found myself tinkering at the various options and builds for an hour!
Well, after an hour, I thought that the options did not really matter because I wasnt going to play the game given how bad it must be according to the reviews I had read. However, I was still waiting for those cards so I decided to have a look at the actual game.
Again, to my suprise, although it started slowly, the game captured my interest. Slowly, but steadily, I started enjoying the story and the battles gameplay. That was it, after some time I was hooked!
Here is what I think of the game:
+Give the game some time at the beginning. It starts slowly but it steadily builds a strong story! Same goes for the gameplay. It looks a bit strange at first but I grew to like it very much!
+The Graphs are really good.
+Full sound + Voice + Subtitles
+Dialogue options
+Decisions matter
+Challenging game
+Character creation system. There is no level up system - Using adventure points to create unique ways of fighting.
+Story twists.
+I havent encountered any in game bugs.
-Some may find the game TOO challenging. Its not a forgiving game. You have to think the consequences of your gameplay.
-Linear. Most of the times there is only one battle available.
-THE MOST IMPORTANT PROBLEM AT THE MOMENT IS THAT THE GAME SEEMS TO HAVE SOME PROBLEM RUNNING IN WINDOWS 10. However, this issue can be solved with a little bit of tinkering. There are numerous solutions out there.
To sum up, I fully recommend this game at a discount and even at full price if you enjoy turn based RPGS. I dont understand whats going on with other reviews. Perhaps people were expecting a different kind of game? However, keep in mind that the game has some compatibility issues with Win 10.

I can't have more than an hour into this game, and it's already crashed twice on loading screens. I force-quit it on the third non-tutorial level.
I'm a big fan of daedalic, and I champion myself as being well versed in every turn based RPG of this nature. But this feels like it was never play-tested. It genuinely feels like no one sat down and played it, as a game, and said "okay, these elements work mechanically, but from a game-perspective, they dont." Every single time you miss a hit, and your enemy never misses at all, and you sit there for a dozen turns soaking up damage for what feels like--no strategic reason, you realise, "Oh great, this is one of those games where I need to return to town every ♥♥♥♥ing time I finish a level, to heal up"
Why? Why not just heal back to full between missions? What purpose does returning to the inn after every mission serve as an improvement to the pacing of the game? If you take a bow for your caster (I mean, that makes sense right, you've read the reviews, you know you're gonna run out of mana and you're a ranged character) and you switch to it, and "Oh, I'm pointblank range with this monster. Hit chance 25% 4dmg" monster has 20 hp. Wtf. So statistically it should take me 20 ♥♥♥♥ing turns to kill this? I'm not talking about this being late game and you made a series of bad choices. This is the first mission that doesn't hand-hold you through a required tutorial.
Turns out, yes. It's going to take you twenty ♥♥♥♥ing turns to do anything, while trying to negotiate the ridiculous gimmick (plug those lice holes! Pull those levers!) no. I was done. The game is not balanced in any satisfying way. It's not "challenging". At best, it just challenges your patience to see how many times you can watch your ridiculously weak spell miss for the 20th time, before you realise there's absolutely no pay-off. I understand miss and dodge mechanics. But when your game is structured around you missing more than 50% of the time... there's no fun in that. No one is sitting at home playing this game thinking "Oh oh oh, I missed! What fun! That's 3 in the row!"

So let me start this review with a story, and a few notes first, and then go into just listing the pros and cons. I went into this with playing Single Player, I had fun, but I will admit that I had used cheats because I had based next to an enemy base and until I would move, I would have kept getting attack, so I just which made it not as fun as SP with that unintentional feeling that I could cheat. Anyways Singleplayer was definitely not bad, and let me note that this game is good and I would recommend it but the next part is technically the whole reason why I'm not. Do note that this isn't just because I had a bad experience, this is because each time that I've had played games that had toxic communities, they all started with having a bad experience and every time after that, it would give me a bad experience.
So after playing SP, I tried Multiplayer, and I found a server that I thought I could definitely play on because it only said PvE, nothing intended to raid, steal, backstab, etc... aka like a Co-op server. I get on their, ask if I could join a faction, someone replies and lets me into their faction. We did some trust bonding, I had to go afk a few times, and everything seemed fine. Then we decided to go mining, but I was requested at a certain time to check on something, but we were still flying to the planet. When I came back from checking on what I needed to check, I was found to be kicked out of the faction, on a planet that's not habitable and no basic materials that I had to get to be able to play on the server. Luckily with nothing stolen but some meat that I was farming with their equipment anyways. But it still was a backstab, and completely uncalled for, and definitely an immature thing to do. So I tried to get the user who did this all reported, but in return, I was just told "It's my server, I can do what I want" so I was like okay, that's not a good mindset, but since I didn't lose anything, I only needed a TP. So giving a second attempt at finding a faction, I join another one who proclaims to be a serious faction. This time I actually had put stuff in the boxes because I was trying my hardest to give trust again. But my game starts freaking out and requires me to restart the game. When I come back, nothing is said, and I get distracted by watching a video. I come back to find that I was kicked out of the base, but not the faction. We had a pointless argument, a lot I would say seemed irrelevant from the opposing side, but we came to an agreement. So we went on with business, and then I had to go afk. I mean IRL stuff can get in the way sometimes when you play games, but being that this is a survival game, where no time was being wasted, nothing bad was happening, and me telling the players of the faction that I had to go afk, I come back to seeing that I was kicked out of this faction as well. At this point, I was just at the point between being mad, and being angry, because this is just idiotic and immature. But everything cools down for a few minutes, another player offers their faction, and I thought maybe I can try 1 more time. But by the time I could do anything, for no significant reason, no warning, no reason, absolutely nothing, I was banned both from the server and the Discord.
So to just sum up what my Multiplayer experience was like, it was just basically a bunch of backstabbing all in one day. Mind you that this is a PVE server, not a PvPvE, or a PvP/PvE, purely PvE. With this, and prior experiences, I just concluded that the games community is as toxic, if not worst, then most survival games. If you think Ark was bad, this is just worst in terms of the community.
So to list overall about this game and a conclusion to all this, here are the pros and cons of this game:
Pros:
(-) Lots of space
(-) Is pretty easy to learn, I would say I learned half of the game (at least) in 1 day.
(-) Challenging, but not too challenging
(-) Kind of seamless out of planet/into planet into/from space
Cons:
(-) Kind of unoptimized
(-) The community seems to be toxic for Multiplayer experiences, only very few actual friendly players (for the people who don't just like to PvP)
(-) Has some unnecessary restrictions for things like Sp, even though it's not restricted in creative.
In conclusion, I do recommend this game IF you are ready to either play with a friend you do actually trust, by yourself, or you just want to play the Singleplayer experience. I strongly suggest to not try and join any faction, PvP or not, that you don't know about, or you could just get backstabbed. I know it kind of seems like common sense, but mind you that these people were giving me stuff and that also implied that I should trust them, let alone a PvE server is, again, meant to be basically working with players, not trying to steal or take from them, which is a PvP type experience.

Ok. Where do i start on this game? Although it appears that I have low play time on this game I actually played a hell of a lot of this game before I was on steam. This game is nuts, but you know..... fun nuts. The maps in this game are fun with not too many camping spots (as if you would feel the need to anyway) and are mostly quite large.
Now....... The guns. Ok, so first up is the Machine Gun which is only good if you are accurate and your enemy is very inaccurate so lets skip this one. Then there is the Shotgun. One hit kill at short range of course and good damage at medium range. The Rocket Launcher is deadly to both your enemy and yourself but can also tend to take a few hits to kills if not hit directly. The Plasma Gun is basically a super Machine Gun. It has a lot more damage and similar fire rate. the Grenade Launcher in my opinion is the hardest gun to use because you have to time as well as place the grenade well. the Railgun, my favourite weapon, is basically a sniper that you have to no scope with (except unlike no scoper's in COD it actually takes skill) and is either a one or two hit kill. The Lightning Gun shoots out a stream of lightning towards your enemy and does decent damage. It's kind of like a Super Soaker except instead of water coming out there's lightning. And finally there is the BFG10K. now this gun is a one hit kill and has a fast automatic fire rate so it kicks♥♥♥♥♥♥
Now in addition to these guns is the gauntlet, which is basically a glove with a spinning saw blade on it. Its usually a two or three hit kill but its always fun to kill someone with it. also there are several other items that can be placed on the maps such as +5, +25 and +50 health capsules, +5 armour shards, +50 and +100 armour vests, a mega health capsule, a quad damage power-up, as well as a regeneration power-up and a beast power-up. I won't take the time to explain these items (Most of which are pretty self explanatory anyway). The best piece of advice that I can give you is to aim well. You aim well and you win....
Anyway I thoroughly reccomend this game to all and I hope this review helps.

You can enjoy this game but there is a better alternative. Motogp 15.
Short reveiew: From the racing point of view, a decent game with realistic and professional gameplay. There are issues with sound and graphics.
Long review:
I am a fan of motogp games and i have realy enjoyed this game. Motogp 14 is a bike racing simulation with realistic physics. There are real names (marquez, rossy...) and the game has enough tuning variety to include you into details.
Pros:
- Realistic game. Hardcore game :D
- Tuning is literaly the key to win or lose a race.
- There is an assistant to help you with tuning.
- There is a career mode where you can start from scracth and make your way up to being a teammate of valentino rossi.
- There is a championship mode, where you can actually be valentino rossi :D
- There is a historic battles mode where you play as a 2013 rider in a historic situation like moving from the 4th place to 1st.
- There is a challenge the champion mode where you have to do better than your opponent, most of the time a champion.
Cons:
- Antialiasing is weird. The game has graphical issues. I have resolved it by overriding the game settings with ati driver settings.
- The sound is cool but it feels inconsistent. Maybe it is because i am not familiar with it.
- The game forgets the control layout of joypad. I have to configure it everytime i open the game.
- The game requires Alt + Tab and task manager force kill to be closed when playing with gamepad.
If you have this game, don't buy motogp 15 and get used to weird sound and override graphic options from driver. You would like this game as a bike racing game. If you have motogp 15, do not waste your time or money on this.

Welcome to my review of Gloria Victis, The medieval MMO made by a small team of 12 employees from Poland.
Please do keep in mind this game is FAR from finished. its playable and you can easily sink alot of hours into the game.
But not all features planned are in this game. #stillInAlpha
GV:
Right now we are playing in stonehelm. a small island off the coast of Logres. With alot of signs of the land being at war for years. 3 Factions are present here and PVP can be found anywhere. 3 main towns. 3 main millitiary keeps and about 14 castles yielding different resources are scatterd around the map whom you and some friends can siege to take over. BEWARE the current owners might not like you hacking away at theyre doors!
Pro`s
- Big map. rich with history and easter eggs (Go Geralt)
- A very wide variety of crafting options
- A dedicated team that has brought forth updates to the game EVERY WEEK (Most were not solely bugs)
- Classless system. Based on you`re stats (Which you can change at any time) you can change in whatever class u would
like. Any weight is viable so whatever you like is okay!
- One of the better Soundtracks.
- Beautifull effects with Castles and SunShine
- Community RP`s for a fair bit. Most guilds have realised that experienced commanders who know what to do in every
situation has become crucial!
- Tactics and Working togheter is promoted alot.
- A medium depth combat system (Medium thx to Bugs VS the different weapons)
- Market offers a nice extra part of the game. Price wars have been going on since day 1.... BUY ALL THE BAGS! NOW
SELLEM!
- Goofy helpfull community. You do need to be social.
- Alot of group PVE content
Cons
- Bugs. Theyre here. You might fall somewhere, but you will be able to get out easily.
- Combat might feel sluggish or not responisve at some points
- Jumping over players and ignoring hits can be done (Although you will lose all stam and die anyway.... but still)
- A medium depth combat system (Medium thx to Bugs VS the different weapons)
- You NEED to be social.
- Lacking high level PVE solo content.
Welp pro`s cons and a bit of a story with it. I can really recommend this game. the Pro`s outwheigh the cons.

It's stuff that people rated the game as positive seemed to enjoy, so I'm gonna whine about it here via making a review, and hopefully get booty blasted for a month or few by people in the comments of this review. C:
To start, the gameplay and menu design feel like a mobile game to me for some reason.
The UI feels very touch-screen designed, and you have to replay levels but under specific contrainsts to gain 'medals' which are basically challenges for the levels. I don't really like how the progression is based around getting these medals. I don't think it's a bad thing persay? It's just not for me.

Let's make a Hypothetical (In other words, not an actual in-game thing) example: Challenge one is say; to kill all the enemies in the level.
Challenge two is to take no damage, sounds reasonable enough right? But then the last one is beat the level in under 20 or 30 seconds.
I'm not expecting to be able to do that in one attempt, of course not. That would be really stupid of me.
I don't... Really like replaying levels just to unlock things though? I'd rather just continue with the game, but this is how you unlock upgrades for purchases. Not really a fan of that either.
If you don't get medals, you're stuck with a very limited number of upgrades to choose from.
So if you like that kinda thing? Get it I guess? Because that seems to be the gameplay loop.
>Beat levels >Replay them for challenges to unlock new abilities and passives >Repeat process.
I haven't tried the multiplayer because it seems to be local co-op only? I could be wrong though but I never saw a online multiplayer thing? So don't get it if you want to play it with your friend across the country or w/e if that's the case.
Also, the protagonist uses text to speech that made my ears bleed, and I really didn't want to sit through that for the entire game.
For those who are severely autistic like me about the TTS voices. I forgot the name of this particular one, but it's used in that abomination called "Go Animate!"
Whenever I hear the protagonist say anything, I immediately am reminded of those cringe inducing Caillou 'animations' that someone 'made' in Go Animate.
Like c'mon guys, at least use the one Limit Breakers use. I'd be laughing my head off to hear that old man voice.
But yeah, I dunno. The game is cheap and there isn't a neutral review option. But I don't think the game is worth $15.
I'd buy it for $10 if it was the base price (and if it wasn't on sale.)
I did refund it because I just wanted to try it out and ended up not liking it. I was recommended it via Steam tags because I REALLY dig character customisation.
It does in the build sense, but you can't make your own cyborg dude at all. You're just adding passives onto him and changing how his gun works. That's about it.
I'm also very amused by the people comparing this to Hotline Miami. I don't think we need another "This is the Dark Souls of X genre".

Not perfect but bloody good.
The game is extremely addictive, you will be screaming at your screen at times in frustration for missing a time limit or because one of your hostages decided to run into a mine but then you will literally cheer as you beat an objective.
The game makes you replay levels, you cant just go through doing the bare minimum objective wise or you will not be able to unlock new levels, you have to achieve as much as possible on each level in order to minimize replaying levels to meet objectives you missed and at times it can be really frustrating when you need a point more to unlock a level and the objectives you have left to finish on your older levels are all really difficult.
I love how you can upgrade your character and your gun, theres a perk like system and in the case of the gun you also get firing types that you can upgrade, for example you can have the gun in shotgun mode and upgrade it from doing spread damage of 7 x 200 to 7 x 400 or you can change the ammo type to laser and do a single blast of 200 damage, it is entirely up to your play style. the same goes for character perks, you can aim to make your character a stealth warrior or a death machine, you may actually need to change your setup in order to meet objectives.
the game does however have flaws, one is that as mentioned the hostage AI could do with some upgrades, they run into enemy positions when a clear route exists, they run into mines, they just generally could be a lot better, it would also be nice if the story was a bit more indepth, it feels very shallow, the game is an obvious nod to judge dread and while that is by no means a bad thing, would of liked to of seen a bit more story to this.
Overall one of my favourite little games in my selection, its not going to win any awards but it is a solid and addictive game that can give you a few hours of enjoyment. That being said I would wait till a sale to buy it purely because it is only a small quite short game and is not going to give you hundreds of hours of gameplay

Do you like stealth games that completely discourage you from completing the game in any other fashion other than undetected? Then play Styx: Master of Shadows. The game will not hold your hand, it will not give you crazy powers that you can use at will multiple times, and it will most of all not forgive you for getting caught. The enemies will not be as dumb in this game, so sneaking past them without raising suspicion is a priority in the gameplay. Sometimes, you might end up being detected by an enemy without even realising where he was in the first place, though. The additional challenges add more things to do, but may at times be discouraging due to how tedious completing them might be. The atmosphere, however, is the best of all, as this game will make you a bit nervous in some parts and maybe a bit frustrating in others. All in all, if you want to play a more challenging stealth game that only allows stealth and will keep you constantly aware of your surroundings as you play it, then this is the game for you.

This may be the only review I ever write for a game (because I know for a fact that I haven't written one on Steam yet), but this game hit pretty hard for me. Although I can't say that I had a personification/imaginary friend that I took to adulthood, I do know what it's like to see the world through a negative perspective. When Faye always pointed out how Colin is such a downer, I never thought much of it more than an observation. But then when she took full control of his memories and merely shifted them to include the happy memories he made instead of his previous memories that mainly focused on his regrets and mistakes in the later half of his life, it shook me to the core. Because in this game, for me, no major change in Colin's life was made at all, but rather, Faye just gently nudged his memories so that they included the good that sprung from his decisions instead of having him focus on what went wrong in his life, which now seem comparatively trivial in hindsight. Did Colin accidentally spill his drink on his honeymoon? Sure, but he then learned about the usefulness of invisible ink, which he made great use of afterwards. Did Colin hire the wrong guy who can't seem to spell anything for his proposal? Perhaps, but she still married him regardless and loved him deeply for decades afterwards.
SPOILERS END HERE
Although I can't say I shed any tears for this game (although, the more playthroughs I watch of the game, the more tears I shed, so this statement is no longer valid :P), it definitely hit me where I didn't expect it to hit. When I initially approached this game, I was hoping to have my lacrimal glands destroyed to oblivion. What I got instead was unexpected but also extremely refreshing. As with its prequel, I'd fully recommend this game and am recommending at the moment to anyone, both video game enthusiasts and non-enthusiasts alike. After all, I believe that there's a lesson or two we can always learn from games produced by Kan Gao and FreeBird games and that it doesn't require the most in-depth game mechanics to craft a compelling story, as you have all proved time and time again.
As for the soundtrack, once again, this OST has knocked the ball out of the park yet again. I watched both trailers for this game and was so hyped that I would repeatedly return to them hoping that the story and music will deliver (which they both did). I could never imagine playing any of these games without a tear-jerking theme in the background to match the ambience of the story. There is even a part in the game where music from the first trailer of "Finding Paradise" kicked in, and I was blown away that it took so long to make its appearance. The occasion it was queued for, however, was very fitting. I will definitely purchase the soundtrack for this game, as I have for the first, but that will have to wait until my wallet fills up again.
Until then, I look forward to the next artful masterpiece that will come out and spend the rest of my time acting on the ideas that were presented to me in this delightful game.

It's an alpha first/third person survival sandbox building game with a space theme.
Developers are very active, multiple updates every week is common.
Things that are working fine already:
- Mining, you can modify terrain, build many kind of mining devices, mine rocks, underground minerals, meteorites, asteroids, etc.
- Building. You can build space ships and bases anywhere you want, use different blocks, materials, lights, devices and textures. There are even simple logic system in place. Take a look of workshop to get the idea.
- Exploring, multiple planets and moons and there's stuff in space too.
- Survival.
- Leveling system, while not complicated it's a nice extra feature.
- Combat system is OK too.
Things that are not working fine yet:
- Bugs. Everywhere.
- Multiplayer. It's a mess because of bugs. Luckily the server selection screen is so broken that it's almost impossible to join to any server anyway.
- Placeholders. There are features, for example some NPCs, that are introduced to the game but not yet working. It's of course nice to see what's probably coming in the future but at the same time those features can break the immersion.
Overall, I would say that it's a decent game and worth your money especially if you like to build things.

An amazing remake with some rather unfortunate issues.
On one paramite we have a very succesful attempt at making a very faithful remake of Oddworld: Abe's Oddysee - a great puzzle/cinematic platformer game from 1997. It's so good and so close in level layout and design, that it pretty much makes it completely unnecessary to play the original anymore - something that only a truly good remake can do. Everything that was great already was left as is. Everything that required some updating and rebalancing was changed. Quicksave is a huge timesaver and works rather well with a gamepad. Some control changes were an absolute must, so some changes are here straight from Exoddus and some are completely new. Gone is the screen-by-screen level design in a surprisingly smooth transition to the more dynamic camera built levels, which still kept their original layouts almost as is. And the game, at it's best, looks better than the pre-rendered assets from 1997 (which, if not for the resolution, would've still looked good, though).
Sadly, in some things it feels like the devs just went overboard, and in some things it feels like they weren't experienced enough. So while the game does look better than the original at it's best, sometimes you notice very muddy texture work, weirdly boring lighting and not very high-poly models that simply don't look as good as the pre-rendered stuff of the original or just misses the mood of the original a bit. Notably, all the very dark areas that focused on just black shapes/shadows moving in contrast to a more light background, now look much lighter and with more "realistic" lighting, which makes them look less memorable. Also, the game manages to often feel surprisingly badly optimised and demanding more than it looks like it should. Given the lack of noticable loading screens and rather fast transitions, quicksaves and restarts, some thing can be understood and forgiven, but still.
Especially when some outright weird things get noticed. Like - apparently, this game is one of those rare games that doesn't have xinput controller support for the range of xinput-compatible hardware, but instead only for the 360 for windows controller. Even xbox one controller can create issues, from weird control behavior, to crashes. Those can be fixed, but are still simply weird to see in 2014-2015. And if the Alf's escape DLC is any indication of Just Add Water skills of making new gameplay content, then it's especially sad, because that DLC feels like a dump of all the gameplay elements without anything truly interesting and creative to it - something that the main game is full of. And while we are on topic of gameplay - there is a weird change in number of mudokons you have to save - there's 200 more of them now. Can't say that I feel that change justified, except for the sake of saying that 300 feels more like factory crew than 100, maybe?
But anyway, it's still a fun and fantastic game about running, jumping, farting, giggling "hello-follow-me"-ing and narrow escaping. As a huge fan of Exoddus (which I prefered over the original), I hope to see that one treated same or even better.

As of 2016-06-26 the game has been patched really well; it looks great and plays great, even on my Medium PC.
I've already played through the game on console but re-bought it for my PC after a recent Steam sale. The game is more or less the same except that it looks better on PC, since I can increase the settings a fair deal, and it also seems to have been patched more or better than on console.
What's different from MotoGP 13 is that the physics is noticeably different, the bike is trickier and more technical to handle, which I see as a big improvement. I play sim games partly for the technical challenge. There are more game modes as well in MotoGP 14, and more content overall, than in the previous game.
The physics is not as sim-like as in Milestone's SBK games, yet is still challenging enough to be fun and rewarding.
There's a huge amount of content considering each bike model handles differently from the rest, and you have three MotoGP classes. The DLCs add even more bike models to play around with. So contents galore !
In summary, a really good MotoGP game, it has enough changes and new content to make playing it really worthwhile.

I\'m not a big multi-player person, mostly because I suck at them.  But this is addicting.  It\'s a competitive footracing game, with moving obstacles and randomized race tracks.  There is no single player mode, but there\'s also nothing here that would make it necessary.  The visuals are neat, I really like the designs and colors they went for here.  There\'s a view for 1st or 3rd person, also which is nice, you don\'t see options too often.  I prefer 1st person myself.  It\'s fast paced and a bunch of fun.
You can get in and out of races really quick, so you\'re not stuck wasting time not playing.  You get different powers that you can use to trip up your opponents, which can sometimes change the outcome of the race entirely.  I still suck at MP, but found myself winning a couple rounds here and there, just due to some well timed powers and luck.  You get a freeze power which freezes you in your tracks, another power which reverses your controls, and also one that makes you slide everywhere like there\'s oil slicks on your feet.  You also have a shield that you can use to deflect attacks if you time it right.
All that with the randomized tracks and moving obstacles make this a fun challenge.  It\'s not contending for any GOTY awards, but it\'s definitely worth the $10 and it\'s a fun distraction that doesn\'t require a lot of commitment.  I\'m looking forward to seeing what else they do with this.  Get a group of your friends together so you can scream obscenities at each other over skype or whatever and it\'s a blast.

Cons:

Honestly, I've read a lot of the negative reviews here on Steam, and most of them complain that the game is too difficult, and in fact, it's just poorly designed and they had to make it so that you can save anywhere to make up for the poor level design.
THAT IS RIDICULOUS.
Yes, the game does have some difficult platforming challenges... But this is intentional, and the save system complements this. You respawn in a fraction of a second and you don't get that helpless feeling of being dead and having to wait for it to load again, like in a lot of games.
Super Meat Boy is another extremely challenging game that does this well: the levels are small but the challenge is huge, but you die and respawn so quick that you're never sitting around waiting.
And just like Super Meat Boy, when you finally do get through a really tough section it feels so rewarding.
I'd much rather die repeatedly in one spot for 3 minutes then have an entire game that doesn't challenge me.
The game only took 10 hours to beat, which is surprising because it felt like much more. It's a big world and the complexity builds nicely throughout the game. But I know for sure this is a game I will play over again and again.

I got the game for free some weeks ago(maybe months?) and since my GPU bite the dust around the same time I kept it on my flash drive and took with me so I could play at home and university,  got some mods installed and started it up, made a INT and CHR based character and had I tough start.
The game is turn based, with action points to spend on each action you make, shooting, walking, looting, inventory management, reloading, the list goes on, your character is created on 2 main systems, S.P.E.C.I.A.L.
Every attribute of S.P.E.C.I.A.L can make a difference when you're chatting with NPCs, maybe you're a really burly dude/dudette and wants to threaten a hobo for some information, the problem is, you really can't say what stats you're using since sometimes it may be not as intuitive as the example.
And skills are your practical actions, sneak, repair things, picklock, heal yourself, etc, the game is an open world RPG with a really generous time limit, if you're like me and got PTSD from Majora's Mask, don't worry, you'll hardly notice the time limit, you'll be travelling the waste lands up and down and while questing and chatting with townsfolk all around, some characters even have a more detail chatting interface, they are really well made and help settle the tone of the game.
Most of the game is pretty boring, I'd probably blame it on the landscape since to make everything dead and unhappy you gotta use a lot of the same colors and don't use too many details on places that are not very special, that said the vaults, cities and a few end-game places looks great, with a lot of detail and life given to it by NPCs and computers.
Some NPCs even have a detailed face that pops up when chatting with them, it's really well made and fun to watch them blab away.
The ambient music is okay, never really cared for it, it set the mood right, that said the sounds of weapons and explosions are oddly satisfying, the explosions and sounds of miniguns blasting away feels really good!
I had a blast with the game, although sometimes the enemies crit a little too often, I'd specially recommend the game to players who's only knowledge of the series comes from 3 and on, you'll be surprised to know where the series roots come from.
Thank you for reading my review, I'll even drop a hint for you kind people, don't save mid-battle, the game will corrupt the save data, this apparently happens on Fallout 1 and 2.

Coming back to this game after years and years of having forgotten all about it, is what I can best describe as a mix of nostalgia and satisfaction. Nostalgia because you recall the endless hours of a great game being played (mostly LAN's), and satisfaction because it actually still holds up against games of the current times, in terms of gameplay. If you're tired of either COD or BF, but still enjoy FPS'es, and you've not tried Quake III Arena, then you should do so.
All the weapons in this game are pretty much available from the beginning, but this is not significant. What is however, is the fact that you really need to learn how to do things in this game. Motion and control has several levels that can be learned, e.g., rocket jumping, circle jumping, strafe jumping, etc. and these are all important for your survival. There's of course all the weapons too. Knowing how to fire a railgun is an important skill. If you meet superior opponents, and you lack these aforementioned skills, you will suffer, and quickly...
I really recommend this game if you want to try a classic that still has something to offer to those who wants some intense FPS action.

You play the titular Jydge (pronounced "judge" with a dystopian Y), a dreadful robotic cop sent in to rescue hostages, defuse bombs, and slaughter gang members across nineteen stages. On its surface, it's a twin stick shooter based around completing various objectives in seemingly small levels. But boy, is there more than a surface here.
There are thirty-five player modifications, fourteen weapons, thirty weapon mods, and fifteen secondary weapons you can unlock. Each level seems small, but they're dense with intersecting paths, multiple entrances, pockets of darkness, and destructible walls and barriers. All of this means that there's an absurd range of possible solutions to every problem. A single mission could be solved by walking through the front door guns blazing, or stealthily sniping from the shadows, or hacking through a back way, or converting enemies to fight for you, or
and running through walls, turning enemies into pulp with a swing of your Gavel. (Gavyl?)
valiantly condenses the complex interplay of an immersive sim into an arcadey shooter. Of course, this is still made by 10tons, with all the bullet dodging and ultraviolence that entails. But
aspires to be something deeper than that, which it tries to convey through objectives and setups that force you to constantly retool your Jydge for the task at hand.
But that's where it gets controversial. At its core, this is a game about replaying. Every level has four difficulties with increasingly harder layouts and their own set of three objectives (one primary, two secondary). Each objective in a level gives a medal, and medals are needed to unlock more levels and upgrades. It's often not possible to get both secondary objectives in one playthrough, so many times a level will need to be beaten twice per difficulty if you want to get everything. Curiously, there are certain elements in a level that carry over between playthroughs; doors that are locked need a key, but will stay open once they're unlocked, and there are certain named enemies that function like minibosses, but they'll stay dead once they're killed. Often, these will get in the way of completing secondary objectives, so you'll sometimes need to unlock those doors and kill those enemies in an earlier playthrough to achieve the objective in a later replay.
What this all means is that if you want the full experience of the game, you'll be diving into the same levels over and over to complete them differently each time. There isn't too much of this if you just want to see the end of the game, and there's a newly-added option to greatly reduce the number of medals needed to get to the end if you're seriously allergic to replaying. But it should also be said that
's soul is in experimenting and discovery, and the changing objectives and layouts are designed to push you out of your comfort zone to see the depths that the game's design offers.
Among twin stick shooters,
is in a class of its own. Its design boldly tries to swing with the greats while still keeping the roots where it came from. If you want a twitchy shooter where you also flex your brain, or if you just want a break from your typical roguelike-shooter/high-score-chaser/whatever, this is well worth your time.

Very good blend of Robocop/Judge Dredd silliness with a nice addictive loop. You'll replay scenarios with different approaches and loadouts to tick off more objectives, and the medals earned are the key to unlocking later levels. It gets a bit hairy around the 45-medals gate, where getting that last couple can be frustratingly difficult, but you're earning more money all the time. Replay some levels, put your focus on money, and upgrade your weapons. I found it best to stick to upgrading just Ion and a lead weapon only. If you spend money upgrading a whole load of weapons, you are likely to hurt your success given that you can only use one at a time.
Some people think it's too much like (the excellent) Neon Chrome on which it's based, but I think the tactics and pacing are genuinely different here.

Jydge is a game developed and published by 10tons Ltd.

I picked this up on a lark, when it was on sale. I'm glad I did! It is amazingly fun, and I'd advise it to anyone looking for something good, fun, and challenging. A lot of people are comparing this to Judge Dredd. Fluff-wise, it's kinda fair, since your character is "Judge, Jury, Executioner" and all that fun stuff, but crunch-wise, it feels closer to the old Crusader games.
There are a few things that have turned people off to the game, and I'll go over them here:
The progression is locked behind "medals"; level-by-level achievements for completing the levels in certain ways, like not killing any civilians, not breaking anything (ASTOUNDINGLY hard), or not being spotted. My advice if you are trying to do this would be to go after the medals oe at a time. Some of them have a nice synergy where you can get more than one in a single run-through easy. Others, not so much. The cyberware that helps with one medal won't help much on another.
A second sticking point is that there's not a whole lot of story. The overarching plot basically boiling down to "get rid of this one particular gang" and the story mostly being told as a radio voiceover played with a spinning graphic image. Yeah, if this were a bigger budget game from a bigger studio, there would probably be a huge, expensive cutscene showing gangers breaking into places and causing mayhem or whatnot, but IMO the resources were better put to making the game more fun. Plus, those cutscenes are usually only watched once, then skipped entirely every other time (the radio messages are skippable, FYI. No unskppable cutscenes in this game).
So if you're looking for a fun, easy in-and-out game, then give it a try! You might be pleasantly surprised.

Let's start out with saying Captain Titus is a badass and he'd still be a badass even if he never was a Space Marine. But lucky for us, he is! So that means Badassius Titanius gets to play with toys that are too brutal for videogames. F*ck that, this is Space Marine, even if it's the Ultrasmurfs.
Jokes aside, Single Player pits you in the skin of Captain Titus. The story is a bit predictable, the Orcs are attacking, but you don't really care anyway. This is Space Marine and you have a duty to do. Which is to brutally slaughter Orcs in the most gratuitous way, largely. I won't spoil who the secret enemies are who will start attacking you late-game. (CHAOS MARINES SHHHHH)
Health packs are for Heretics. You regain health by stunning an enemy and using a finisher on them.
You can carry four firearms, whereof two can be swapped out as you so desire. The array of firearms is classical, with every typical playstyle covered sooner or later. The weapons rarely feel underpowered, but you do have a sense of "wrong place, wrong weapon" at times, which urges you to keep a weapon variation based on distances. Something for close, something for far.
Three melee weapons, whereof the Hammer limits your firearm usage to your sidearm or bolter.
Melee feels strong and satisfying. Whenever enemies get close, you'll feel like you can rely on melee to finish them off relatively easily. Using the hammer makes you prone to rush in and tear them up, a tactic better fitting with Orcs or equipped with a Jetpack (which is only available on specific areas, sadly)
If anything, Single Player makes for a great tutorial on how to handle Multiplayer, which is pretty unforgiving.
Multiplayer is pretty much how you imagine Space Marines going at it. It's big, it's harsh and a little bit quick, as your health does not match that of Titus.
All the weapons you encountered in the Singleplayer are present, and an extra melee weapon if you bother to buy it's DLC for it. The way you go about choosing weaponry is unusual and interesting.
You start out with just one class. Which is the classic Bolter. BUT, you can copy the weapon loadout of the person who killed you. No requirements. If you got killed by a guy with a jetpack, copy it and get some payback. Respawning is fast too.
This balances out with being only possible once. Dying again only makes you able to copy that killer's loadout, or pick a class.
Reaching level 4, you'll unlock two things.
First, a customization slot, allowing you to put together your own class type(normal, heavy or jet♥♥♥♥♥) with the unlocked weapons available to that class type. Then you can read up on the weapon specs and the available (locked or unlocked) perks a class can have. They are various, and many complement a different playstyle with the same class. Variety is endless, and I'm sure that, having unlocked enough over time, you can cater to your own playstyle.
Secondly, you can customize your Space and Chaos Marine.
Meaning, you can swap out unlocked armor pieces and color your Space Bad*ss in any way you like. In general, the armor has a primary color for the brunt of it, and a secondary such as for trimming and extremities.
The color availability itself is pretty impressive and funnily applicable. Imagine picking colors for a car in GTA or Saints Row, that's the kind of options you get to deal with. You get Reds, Yellows, Blues, Greens, then Metallic's and all that jazz. It's pretty hilarious how your Space Marine suddenly is painted like a car.
You can also choose the emblem that'll appear on your left shoulder armor. But if you are thinking of coloring your Space Marine in honor of a known existing Space Marine chapter, you shouldn't bother putting in the work. These color schemes are readily available for both Space and Chaos Marines, at no cost or unlocking requirement. Including their emblem.
If you like 3rd person shooters with an emphasis on badassery and without sissy features like crouching or cover-based shooting, then Warhammer 40k Space Marine is right up your alley.

This game is somewhat interesting, but mostly meh, in my opinion. There's gameplay in there (and if you think of every battle like it's a puzzle that needs solving, it becomes even more interesting), but there are a lot of confusing and idiosyncratic elements that hold it back. Blackguards is not a very good game. It's a great example of turn-based strategy gone horribly wrong and just because something uses hexagons doesn't make it inherently worthwhile.
Blackguards is cheaply made. That much becomes apparent as soon as the voice acting starts torturing your speakers. The voice actor for the male main character is weirdly familiar from other budget titles. He's not trying very hard and neither is anyone else. The graphics are also fairly poor. I didn't expect much but it looks incredibly cheap and one has to suspect it was meant to be a tablet title originally. The art direction is also incredibly generic. This game makes Dragon Age look like Zeno Clash.
Most of the game is really just battles. Towns, numerous as they are, serve to buy gear and heal up and not much more. There are side quests but they almost always result in even more combat. You would think a game that contains this much fighting would have deep mechanics but no. There is not even flanking or backstabbing. Most of the weapon abilities make you hit harder or pierce armor in exchange for accuracy and that's basically it for physical attackers. Abilities that can hit multiple enemies are only available very late and they are not great. There is a knockdown but it virtually never works and most elite enemies are outright immune to it. The game is terrible with double standards like this.
Mages have a bit more to do but the spells are horribly imbalanced, ranging from absolutely useless to pretty much necessary to beat the game. You can't even make a proper offensive mage because spells do poor damage and are not very mana-efficient. There's virtually no way to restore mana outside of the very poor regeneration between turns. Potions do exist but they are insanely expensive. They're something you use in a boss fight and not something you can waste in a regular encounter. To make things worse, spells are also line of sight dependent. That means if you surround an enemy with your melee fighters, you can't hit them and if one of your characters gets surrounded you can't heal them. Want to throw a fireball into a cluster of enemies? You can't because you have no line of sight to the center so you can never really hit the whole group. It's as annoying as it sounds. Level 4 spells on the other are insane. They can hit every single enemy or ally on the entire map, no matter how far away they are. Sadly, later on enemies use the same spells against you and it's awful because you can't do anything about it.
The game's biggest downfall are the gimmick maps. This is hard to explain. Basically, half the encounters are built some sort of gimmick except... the game doesn't explain these gimmicks to you or warns you that there even might be a gimmick instead of a regular skirmish. The most blatant example is when you plunder a crypt and you get attacked by a gang of skeletons (you never hear about skeleton gang violence in the media, typical) and every time you destroy one, it gets resurrected by some crystal. Fair enough, you have the skeletons distracted by some of your fighters and have another one sneak around and attack the crystal. You attack it with your spear and...it does no damage. The crystal is immune to thrust damage. There is no feedback to it, you can't figure it out on your own through the environment. Well, that would have been nice to know, I thought to myself. Most of the time the best way to beat is a map is to figure out the gimmick and immediately reload the fight in order to actually use it to its full effect. Everything else is an uphill battle.
So yeah, it's not a very good game. It's full of baffling design decisions and even the things outside of combat are not good. I could write for hours about the awful, incoherent story but it's not worth the effort.

I would not recommend this game to anyone. If you particularly enjoy the Fallout lore, you might enjoy this game, but even then you’d probably get more entertainment reading up on the content of this game from the wiki.
Pros:
If you’ve played a Fallout game before, it’s interesting seeing the origins of stuff, like where the super mutants come from and the first interactions with the Brotherhood of Steel.
Some of the death animations are really cool. The animations for getting a critical plasma kill are better in this game than in Fallout 3 and New Vegas.
That’s all I can think of.
Cons:
The UI is crap, the isometric view is implemented poorly, and the way that your character appears on the screen interferes with your ability to play the game. If you are directly behind a wall or door (so that the door is between your character and the camera), the area that would block your view disappears so that you can still see your character. Fine, but you need to click on doors to open them, and if you are directly behind a door, you won’t be able to see the door to click on it, and the game is very finicky about which part of a door you can click to open it. Actually, the game is quite finicky about where you can click pretty much everything, including menu buttons.
The controls are annoying and unintuitive. Left click does every action and interaction (including movement), right click changes the type of action you’ll be doing with your left click. It doesn’t sound too bad, but your character can’t interpret any commands that require more than one action, so if you click to move to the other side of an unlocked door, your character will freeze and say they cannot get there. Left clicking directly on the door while in move mode doesn’t do anything. You have to right click to change to interact mode, left click the door to open it, right click to change back to move mode, then click to move past the door. If you are in one of the several places in the game where doors automatically close after a couple of seconds, you may need to repeat the process several times per door when your companions block you from moving, or the game decides that you can’t stand on that particular empty hex (it seems to have a problem with hexes that are too close to doorways and walls). If the door is locked, you have to click the skills list at the bottom of the UI, click lockpicking, click the door (making sure to move your character to a position where you can see the damn door), right click to change to interact mode, left click the door to open it, right click to change back to move mode, then left click to move past.

There are also frequent moments in the game when you can (or have to) use your skills on objects (such as the lockpicking skill on a door), and you’ll struggle to because your character is in the way, and repeatedly moving your character so that you can try and use the skill again gets old fast.
The skills are ridiculously unbalanced and poorly implemented. There are 18 skills, and most of them are useless. Speech is hands-down the best non-combat skill, and you’ll use it consistently throughout the game. Lockpick is almost as useful, then there are 1 or 2 skills that you might use once or twice, and everything else is worthless. I did one playthrough (of 35 hours), and I never figured out what the Outdoorsman skill did. The Gambling skill has no value for anything to do with the main game, and even for doing actual gambling you can ignore it if you have a high Luck stat. The First Aid skill seems to work equally as well (i.e., barely does anything) whether you have 30% or 90%. Talking of First Aid, your on-use skills, including First Aid, are activated from a skills menu, but using First Aid (and presumably Doctor, but at no point did I have to use Doctor in my playthrough) from that menu has a 0% chance of doing any healing, because you have to use a first aid kit when doing First Aid, but apparently your character doesn’t know this, because they won’t use a first aid kit that is in their inventory if you tell them to use First Aid from the skills menu. They’ll still attempt to do first aid, and time will still pass, but you’ll always get the message “you failed to do any healing”.
There are 5 types of weapon (with a related skill to determine your effectiveness), but Energy Weapons are objectively better than all of the others so there’s no point in using anything else as soon as you get an energy weapon.
The inventory system is horrible. You can’t tell what anything does or often even see what it’s called unless it’s actually in your inventory (so deciding whether you want to drop things so that you can pick up something you’ve found is a pain), and even then a lot of the descriptions are vague at best. Some things need to be in one of your two item slots in order to use them, some don’t, and it’s not clear until you test each individual thing which of those two categories anything is.
You can’t move money in increments larger than $999, and after you leave the second area, practically everything costs more than that. You don’t know tedium until you’ve payed for $120,000 worth of gear in increments of $999.
Companions are only useful to carry your stuff and because of the crappy inventory system they’re not even very good at that. They're complete morons - they'll wander in a small area around you, but they'll still do this even if they've detected a trap in the area and happily blow themselves up on landmines that they've spotted. They also constantly get in your way, and you can't move them out of way by any means apart from waiting for them to start wandering or killing them. They start out somewhere between weak-and-useless and subpar-and-useless, and seeing as they can’t level up or wear armour they don’t really get any better. You can give them other weapons, but only if they know how to use them, and none of them can use Energy Weapons, so there’s little point. Towards the endgame they’ll die in one hit from most enemies and barely scratch them in return.
TL;DR: Overall, this game was a huge disappointment. I love the Fallout universe, I love CRPGs, I’m fine with old games, but this just doesn’t hold up in any respect. If you’re interested in the lore, read the wiki. If you want to play a good CRPG, play Baldur’s Gate. This game isn’t worth your time.

Set in the aftermath of a world-wide nuclear war, Fallout will challenge you to survive in an unknown and dangerous world. You will take the role of a Vault-dweller, a person who has grown up in a secluded, underground survival Vault. Circumstances arise that force you to go Outside -- to a strange world 80 years after the end of the modern civilization. A world of mutants, radiation, gangs and violence. Your immediate task is to find a replacement for the broken water purification controller chip. Without that chip, your fellow Vault dwellers are doomed to dehydration or be forced to leave the safety of the Vault for the Outside.

From the age of intelligence-respecting games, Fallout stands out as one of the most famous and influential RPGs of the era. It started as a humble project, and became a beloved piece of gaming history, spawning a franchise that, after dying, came back stronger than ever.
Gameplay:
Fallout works on an attribute and skill and perk/trait system. The customization is very high with character creation. There are 7 primary attributes, a bunch of skills, and a handful of traits to choose from at the very start. Like in real life each attribute, skill, and perk/trait has their own use, but some are far better than others.
The core gameplay takes some getting used to, but it's not too complicated. In combat, you have a limited number of action points per turn, and you can spend them however you like, shooting, reloading, using items, or moving. Combat is very punitive, but this goes both ways. The beginning of the game is quite difficult due to starting equipment being quite lame. Outside of combat you can interact with things and people, like any other standard rpg. Dialogs feature choices, which can have dire consequences. Be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, get shot or ignored.
Story:
You are some Vault Dweller being given the simple yet weightful task of getting a water chip. There's no predetermined player character, you are whoever you want to be. From the very beginning, you are your own person. Rather than force a narrative upon the player, characters offer information and their opinions on events in the wasteland giving the player a chance to genuinely care about issues. The only forced narrative is the water chip quest, which serves as an adventure catalyst. It points you in the direction of the rest of the game. You will encounter civilizations and can choose whether or not to get involved with their problems. The intelligence shown in the writing and the respect for the player's intelligence are definite strong points of the game, they will provoke deep thought, including philosophical topics and the ethics of a ruined world.
Graphics/Art:
Moody, grainy, stylish, and isometric, Fallout boasts a distinctive look. At higher resolutions without scaling, it can be an extremely visually noisy game. Every sprite is packed with subtle details. Different civilizations will have a distinct style to their townships, from freshly built adobe buildings to repurposed garbage and pre-war ruins to a perfectly preserved and well-maintained bunker, there's a lot to look at and take in. People all have graphic and sometimes gory death animations, making combat feel satisfying and brutal.
One stand-out feature of Fallout is that major characters have "talking heads," which are creepy, painstakingly detailed facial animations. These are uncanny, but the work put into them is tremendous, and despite looking very weird today they still work quite well, they belong in this post-nuke world, and I have a soft spot for them.
Sound Design:
The soundtrack varies between moody tribal-ish music to very industrial tracks. While many of them aren't what I would call pleasant to listen to, it matches the mood perfectly.
The sound effects are standard for a game like this, I enjoyed them.
Conclusion:
This game holds up well today, getting a patch for modern systems is almost necessary, but the vanilla game is great. It challenges the player in a genuine way, mentally and gameplay-wise. If you enter the game hot off the heels of Fallout 4 you will likely think it's♥♥♥♥♥♥due to the stark difference in pacing and how much patience you need to play, but adjusting to this old fart of a game is well worth it.

Evoland 2 is a celebration of video games over last 30 or so years. Its subsequent genre-shifts and swapping up of game mechanics usually translates to quite a bit of variety, but several of the ideas suffer from lackluster execution (most notably the beat-em-up section, whose controls are awful). That's not to say it can't nail the ideas it gets right. For example, there's an an entire 2-3 hour section that flawlessly emulates a fire emblem campaign, right down to unit construction and multiple paths to reach the final encounter. If that isn't your cup of tea, however, Evoland pretty much covers all the bases. The "default" gameplay is an action RPG (intentionally akin to classic Zelda), but there are homages to sidescrollers, endless runners, platformers, rhythm games, Bomberman, Megaman, Professor Layton, Street Fighter, and the list goes on. My personal favorite was the Hearthstone clone, as it actually requires you to scour the game world to find new challengers and collect better cards.
The story, almost in its entirety, is a spoof of Chrono Trigger. In fact, if you flattened out its library of game mechanics to include only Chrono Trigger's combat system (which it spoofs too at one point), you'd be left with a slightly shorter clone of the big CT. It should be noted, however, that while it's a clone, it's a very GOOD clone; it manages to capture the same sense of adventure, portray similarly lovable characters, and emulate the same fascinating time travel micro-narratives Chrono Trigger was known for. Unfortunately, unlike Chrono Trigger, Evoland 2's story builds up to the reveal of some massive, interwoven, deep backstory, and then ends in a confusing tangle of not answering the questions it asks of the player, and providing scraps of information without any context. If there was some grand, unseen narrative, it needed to be explained explicitly by the end, rather than just hinted at.
Worth mentioning is the humor and surprisingly vast list of references and nods to various game series, as it can be quite hit-or-miss depending on what your tastes are. There were a few times where it was legitimately charming, such as when I slowly realized a certain little girl was dressed like Paula from Earthbound, or when I was forced to work at a burger joint to pay smuggling fees, but it also had a few times where the humor fell flat, like with the sentient "Yoda tree" whose gag is that they talk like Yoda.
Overall, its a fun game, especially if you can appreciate the genre-shifts, but don't expect a very serious experience.

+ The graphics (I'm not sure which)
+ The very simple story and dialogues
+ The puzzles (still hate them though)
+ Open world (I love that about it so much) // But it is open once you almost beat the game which is unfortunate.
+ The story (kind of simple, but simple is good, right?)
+ Very very very much of a cool concept! (Just love how many GAMES are in this GAME!)
+ References (I mean what can I say, If you are a snowman you pretty much know nothing)
+ Pretty funny adventure! (The guards are just very smart, let me tell you that!)
- The freedom (sometimes I just don't know how to hit a bush)
- Feels a little bit unfinished at some places
- No ability to get out of dungeon fast when already beaten
- No clues (not bad thing for everyone, but the puzzles are sometimes too much for my brain)
- Buggy on some places
- Not much of options in Options (see what I did there? Anyway, if the game bugs the sounds you pretty much cant do anything)
Overall feeling from the game
Absolutely humongous good feeling, I mean you just play a game where you remember all the fun time you had with games in your life time. You go through so many references and old feels that the game just has a really special place for my heart. Getting through the game was a bit hard but god am I glad to play such a beautiful game! Very good memories will last from this big adventure. Thank god it's finally over. Time to replay it on the hardest difficulty!
Do you recommend this game?
No! How could I not recommend this game. You only just die a lot, scream a lot and bash your head over the table because you forgot to hit that freaking bush. My head hurts and yours will too, so bear yourself.
On a serious note though, the game is definetly not for everyone. If you are looking for some great adventure then here you go! You wont experience much of a combat but it definetly fills up the requirements for a "sit back with beer" game. But just please do not play this game if you have no patience or you're looking for some action, you won't enjoy it. Sorry!
Anyway I hope if you DO buy this game, you will have a great time like I did. Just don't give up on the first obstacle. Get it through your head and you will be fine. Sometimes even I forget to flip a freaking lever right next to me(still hate myself for loosing one hour of a god damn time for my stupidity, so don't be stupid).
If you read this far you are one of a crazy or a very bored person but I love you for that! Have a great fun playing games! Cheers.
PS: Watch out for the great Destroyer who brings the Great Disaster!
